story: At 8:17 on a sunny Thursday evening in Sumter Oaks, Gary is at the Town Hall architectural review desk filing his golf cart lights and sound system request, with the 10 PM cutoff noted in careful handwriting. Out on Magnolia Loop, Donna is in good spirits, promising two dozen deviled eggs and declaring she is finished with the flamingos, three out front and the rest headed to the backyard. Hal and Rosa are settling into an easy evening together, with Hal offering a folding chair in case anyone needs a spare and Rosa confirming dinner at six sharp before heading home to prep.
events: Gary (architectural review desk): File my golf cart lights and sound system modification request, with the 10 PM sound cutoff noted

gary.thought_process: I'm at Town Hall with nobody around, and my goal is the parade cart rig. Exterior modifications visible from the street need Architectural Review approval (L-01), so the sensible move is to use the architectural review desk and get my cart paperwork filed properly. I was just at the parade signup table, so I know the entry rules. Hal already helped me check the lines, and I wrote the 10 PM cutoff for the sound system into the paperwork to stay on the right side of L-03. Time to file it and get it official.

parameters.content: File my golf cart lights and sound system modification request, with the 10 PM sound cutoff noted

donna.thought_process: Rosa asked about allergies for Friday and I haven't answered her yet. Hal is tallying my flamingos, and I already told them both I'm bringing deviled eggs and that Gary's practice is at ten tomorrow. Answer Rosa's question directly with the egg details (eggs and mayo, nothing else), then the conversation can wrap up and I can get on with pulling the flamingos down to three.

parameters.content: No allergies on my end, sweetheart, but my deviled eggs have mayo and mustard in them, so tell anybody who needs to know. I'll bring two dozen, and I'm done with these flamingos tonight, three out front and the rest going out back.

hal.thought_process: Rosa asked about allergies for Friday dinner, and I'm the only one who hasn't answered. I already told her I'd be on time, so I shouldn't repeat that. Donna has promised to get the flamingos down to three, so the clipboard stays put and I'll hold her to her word at dinner. Plain answer for Rosa, a little dry, and it keeps things moving toward Friday.

parameters.content: No allergies here, Rosa. Army cooked for me for thirty years, so my stomach's survived worse. I'll bring a folding chair in case anyone needs a spare.

rosa.thought_process: Donna and Hal both already confirmed Friday dinner, and I've asked about allergies. Donna answered her question to me about Gary's practice tomorrow at ten, and I haven't replied. Hal asked if dinner is still on. I shouldn't re-invite; I should answer them directly, confirm the practice, close the loop, and then head home to prep. Keep it short and warm.

parameters.content: Wouldn't miss Gary's practice, Donna, I'll be there at ten with coffee. Hal, yes, dinner's on, six sharp, so just bring yourself. Now I'm heading home to start prepping.

matters.text: Gary Kowalski: File my golf cart lights and sound system modification request, with the 10 PM sound cutoff noted

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
